summary: Orphaned session after IdP logout/revocation prevents re-login and blocks CI deploys
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers report they are unable to re-authenticate to the Redwood Console after an IdP-initiated logout (Okta) and token revocation event. A subset of these users then trigger CI deploys (via internal CI runner) which fail during service-account token exchange. The session appears 'orphaned' in our session-store: the browser retains a session cookie that the auth-proxy accepts, but downstream services reject due to revoked tokens.

Impact: Multiple CI deploys failed for the infra team (2 blocked deploys in last 6 hours). Several users locked out of web console until a manual cookie clear. Potentially affects any workflow that performs token-exchange (service-to-service operations) when Okta revokes an access token and the session-service does not clean up in time.

Observed behavior: Users see a 403 on the CI job step 'exchange-token' and console shows 'Sign-in required' but the browser still has a console session (stale). Support note: this is not classic 401; the web session superficially looks valid which confuses users and on-call triage.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have a user with an active console session (session cookie + access token in session-store).
2) Trigger IdP-initiated logout from Okta for that user (admin revoke via Okta admin console or use revocation API).
3) Observe webhook delivery from Okta to /webhooks/idp/revocations is acknowledged (200) but session-service does not immediately remove internal session record.
4) User attempts to run CI deploy which performs token-exchange; auth-proxy forwards the stale session cookie, but token-exchange fails with 403 from token-validation service.
logs: 2026-03-10T08:32:14Z session-service WARN cleanup_worker failed to find session by token_id=tok-3f2: race_condition_detected
2026-03-10T08:33:01Z auth-proxy INFO incoming request cookie session_id=sess-41 accepted
2026-03-10T08:33:01Z token-exchange ERROR exchange failed status=403 reason=token_revoked user=matthew@redwood.com request_id=rx-11
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Verified Okta shows revocation events for affected users. Webhook delivery shows 200 from our load balancer logs.

SRE hypothesis: webhook processing acknowledged but session-service hit a transient DB timeout and skipped deletion; session remained in store but marked with revoked=true inconsistent with cache layer.

Found pattern: when webhook and parallel session refresh occur within ~500ms, cache mismatch leads auth-proxy to accept session_id from cookie while token-validation queries identity-service which sees revoked token -> 403.

Reproduction on staging: able to reproduce by issuing revoke and immediately triggering a token-exchange; root cause points to ordering/race between webhook handler, session-store TTL, and the in-memory session cache used by auth-proxy.
Related code areas: session-service deletion path, idempotency for revocation handlers, auth-proxy cache invalidation hooks.
comments: Support (Marta Lopez) 2026-03-10: Customer reports two blocked deploys; asked for logs and browser cookie screenshots.
SRE (Ravi Shah) 2026-03-10: Noted webhook 200s, started a focused runbook to reproduce. Tentatively calling this a race-condition between webhook and cache invalidation.

Platform Eng (Lina Chen) 2026-03-11: Instrumented session-service to emit revocation-handled events to Kafka; observed duplicate delivery in one case causing a transient DB lock. Adding idempotency guard.
Support (Marta Lopez) 2026-03-11: Provided workaround to affected users: clear console cookies or open an incognito window to force full re-auth, and re-run CI. Users confirmed temporary unblock.
resolution: In Progress - temporary mitigation applied (manual cookie clear recommended). Engineering to deploy idempotency and cache-invalidation fix; post-deploy will monitor for recurrence and close the ticket.
next_steps: 1) Push hotfix to session-service: add idempotent revocation handler and explicit cache invalidation event to auth-proxy (PR #4821).
2) Add instrumentation alert when webhook-delivered-revocations are not reflected in session-store within 2s (SLO breach candidate).
3) Run canary in prod-us-west for 2 hours, verify no CI token-exchange 403s correlated with revocations.
4) Follow-up: create a postmortem if recurrence > 1 within 72 hours.
